content.value_statement: AKS design requires early choices that can be hard to change later. This skill guides cluster planning, security, networking, operations, and cost decisions.
actual_capabilities: Recommends AKS Automatic or Standard based on control and customization needs.
Creates Day-0 checklists for networking, API server access, identity, and security choices.
Plans pod IP, ingress, egress, DNS, and network policy options for AKS clusters.
Suggests security controls for Entra ID, Workload Identity, Key Vault, policy, and image governance.
Outlines observability, upgrade, reliability, performance, and cost-control practices.
Provides Azure CLI reference commands for common AKS planning and configuration tasks.
limitations: Requires valid Azure permissions and context before using MCP tools or Azure CLI commands.
Does not replace environment-specific architecture review, quota checks, or compliance approval.
Cannot guarantee zero downtime for upgrades or cluster changes.
May require current Microsoft documentation when Azure AKS features or regions change.

use_cases.title: Design a New AKS Platform
use_cases.description: Build a production cluster plan with SKU, networking, identity, observability, and upgrade decisions documented.

use_cases.title: Review Architecture Tradeoffs
use_cases.description: Compare AKS Automatic and Standard options for control, operational effort, reliability, and cost.

use_cases.title: Prepare Operational Guardrails
use_cases.description: Create practical controls for monitoring, autoscaling, maintenance windows, node pools, and cost visibility.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Cluster
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a dev or test environment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an AKS dev cluster for my team. Ask only for missing essentials, then recommend SKU, region, networking, identity, monitoring, and cost controls.

prompt_templates.title: Compare AKS SKU Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate decision support for platform selection.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare AKS Automatic and AKS Standard for a production workload that needs private networking, autoscaling, observability, and predictable operations.

prompt_templates.title: Design Production Networking
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced Day-0 architecture for connectivity and security.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design AKS networking for a private production cluster. Include pod IP model, API server access, ingress, egress, DNS, and network policy choices.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Operations Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced readiness planning for ongoing cluster operations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an AKS operations plan for upgrades, patching, node pools, reliability, monitoring, security controls, and cost management across environments.

output_examples.input: Plan a production AKS cluster for a web application with private networking and strong observability.
output: Recommendation: use AKS Automatic unless unsupported custom networking requires Standard.
Day-0 decisions: private API server, Azure CNI Overlay, controlled egress, and managed identity.
Operations: enable Container Insights, Managed Prometheus, maintenance windows, autoscaling, and policy safeguards.

output_examples.input: Help me choose between AKS Automatic and Standard for a regulated workload.
output: Automatic reduces operational setup and applies curated defaults.
Standard offers deeper control for strict network, node pool, and add-on requirements.
Decision point: choose Standard only when required controls are not available in Automatic.

output_examples.input: Create a Day-0 checklist for AKS networking and security.
output: Confirm region, zones, subnet capacity, pod IP model, API server access, and egress path.
Use Entra ID, Workload Identity, Key Vault integration, Azure Policy, and approved image sources.
Document choices that require cluster recreation if changed later.

best_practices: Clarify Day-0 decisions early, especially networking, API server access, and identity.
Use managed identity, policy enforcement, approved images, and scoped access for production clusters.
Document tradeoffs for reliability, upgrades, observability, and cost before provisioning.
anti_patterns: Creating a production cluster without confirming subnet capacity, egress design, and API server access.
Using static credentials or broad permissions for pods, nodes, or operators.
Treating dev cluster settings as production-ready without reviewing reliability and security controls.

faq.question: Does this skill create AKS clusters automatically?
faq.answer: It plans and guides AKS configuration. Any cloud-changing action should be confirmed before using MCP tools or Azure CLI.

faq.question: When should I choose AKS Automatic?
faq.answer: Choose AKS Automatic when curated defaults meet your needs and you want less operational setup.

faq.question: When should I choose AKS Standard?
faq.answer: Choose AKS Standard when you need detailed control over networking, node pools, autoscaling, or add-ons.

faq.question: Can it help with private cluster networking?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers API server access, pod IP models, ingress, egress, DNS, and network policy decisions.

faq.question: Does it handle security planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends Entra ID, Workload Identity, Key Vault integration, Azure Policy, image governance, and scoped access.

faq.question: Does it replace Azure documentation?
faq.answer: No. Use it for structured planning, then verify current service behavior and regional availability with official Microsoft documentation.
